skill.name: mantis-history
skill.description: Analyzes repository history to extract past vulnerabilities, security fixes, affected files, and mitigation details into a historical learnings database.
skill.summary: Builds a cached historical security database from repository revisions for downstream analysis.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: All 58 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, legitimate workspace access, or read-only repository checks. A separate semantic risk concerns sending repository diffs and messages to unspecified LLM services without data-sharing safeguards. No evidence found of malicious commands, credential theft, or an actual prompt injection attempt.

remediation.issue: Repository diffs and messages may be sent to unspecified LLM services.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for external processing, select an approved provider, redact secrets, minimize payloads, and offer a local-only analysis option.

semantic_findings.description: The skill requests LLM calls containing commit diffs and messages without specifying provider approval, secret redaction, or local-only processing. External implementations could disclose proprietary code or historical secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly batch diffs and messages into LLM calls but define no data-sharing controls. Actual disclosure depends on the selected execution backend.

content.user_title: Extract Historical Security Fixes with Mantis
content.value_statement: Past security fixes are difficult to track across repository history. This skill guides an AI agent to extract, classify, and cache historical vulnerabilities for later analysis.
actual_capabilities: Inspects repository structure and summaries to identify relevant security issue categories.
Guides generation and execution of a VCS history extraction script.
Filters commit messages and diffs using project-specific keywords and size limits.
Uses batched LLM analysis to classify fixes, affected components, vulnerability types, and mitigation details.
Caches extracted records and checks revision reachability before incremental reuse.
Writes historical learnings with revision identifiers, file references, pass numbers, and timestamps.
limitations: Provides instructions rather than a bundled extractor; generated scripts require an execution environment and accessible repository history.
Keyword filters and skipped large or non-production changes can miss security fixes.
Shallow clones provide partial history; unsupported or inaccessible VCS history produces an empty database with a status marker.
LLM classifications need verification, and external analysis may expose repository content without additional safeguards.

use_cases.title: Prepare Historical Security Context
use_cases.description: Build a repository-specific database of earlier vulnerabilities and mitigations before a broader security investigation.

use_cases.title: Track Recurring Vulnerability Patterns
use_cases.description: Review historical fixes by component and vulnerability type to identify recurring maintenance risks.

use_cases.title: Feed Downstream Mantis Analysis
use_cases.description: Generate state-relative historical learnings with cached records and provenance for subsequent analysis stages.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Summarize Security History
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mantis-history to extract past security fixes from this repository. Report the output location and any history limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: First historical analysis of an accessible repository.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Tailor History Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository's stack and choose relevant security keywords. Extract historical findings and explain which commits your filters may exclude.
prompt_templates.scenario: Project-specific filtering for a large repository.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Refresh Cached Learnings
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh historical learnings from the existing cache. Verify revision reachability and repository identity; rebuild the cache if history was rewritten.
prompt_templates.scenario: Incremental analysis after new commits or a rebase.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Coordinate Snapshot Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mantis-history with --snapshot_root <snapshot>, --snapshot_id <id>, and --state_root <state>. Read live VCS history and preserve snapshot provenance.
prompt_templates.scenario: State-separated analysis within a snapshot-based Mantis workflow.

output: Example finding: An authentication check was added before accessing an account resource.
The historical record links the revision, affected file, vulnerability type, and mitigation.
The conclusion requires verification against the actual revision diff.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Analyze security history from a shallow Git clone.
output: Available revisions were analyzed; older history remains unavailable.
Missing historical findings do not establish that a component is secure.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Analyze a directory without accessible VCS history.
output: An empty historical learnings database was written.

best_practices: Approve the analysis backend and redact sensitive repository content before any external LLM processing.
Keep scripts, caches, and outputs under the designated state workspace, outside the target tree.
Verify extracted findings against their revisions and record partial or unsupported history explicitly.
anti_patterns: Treating an empty or filtered history database as proof that the repository has no vulnerabilities.
Reusing cached findings after history rewrites without checking revision reachability and repository identity.
Sending private diffs or historical secrets to an unapproved external analysis service.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Extraction also requires repository access and an environment capable of running generated scripts.

faq.question: Does this skill review or patch current code?
faq.answer: No. It extracts historical vulnerabilities and fixes. Its stated scope excludes code reviews, test-script creation, and patching.

faq.question: Where are the generated files stored?
faq.answer: With --state_root, scripts, caches, and historical_learnings.jsonl belong under its workspace directory. Without locator arguments, the workflow uses the live working directory.

faq.question: How does it handle missing or shallow history?
faq.answer: Missing or unsupported history produces an empty database marked UNSUPPORTED_VCS. Shallow Git history is analyzed with the PARTIAL_SHALLOW marker.

faq.question: How are repeated runs handled?
faq.answer: The output is rebuilt from cached records. New revisions are analyzed incrementally, and rewritten history or changed repository identity invalidates the cache.

faq.question: Can repository content reach an external service?
faq.answer: Yes, if the selected LLM backend is external. The skill requests diff and message analysis but does not define redaction or provider approval.
